label: Tutorial: who you are browsing as
description: First step of every tour: what the visitor can do, depending on who they are. One entry per role (anonymous, member, admin), plus one line per granted permission (permissions.<key>) for members who hold a role.

anonymous.title: You are browsing as a visitor
anonymous.text:
You can read every public rule and bundle, search, filter and download them.

**Create a free account** to add your own rules, vote, comment, keep favorites, follow people and get alerts.

member.title: You are logged in
member.text:
You can **add rules** (by hand, from a Git repository, a zip or JSON), **build bundles**, vote, comment, keep favorites and propose changes to other people's rules.

You can edit and delete **your own** rules and bundles; for anyone else's, you send an edit proposal that its owner accepts or not.

admin.title: You are an administrator
admin.text:
Everything a member can do, on **every** rule and bundle, plus the **Admin** menu: users and roles, configuration, imports and Git sources, background jobs, connectors to other instances, logs and moderation.

Tours show you the admin parts too: regular users never see those steps.

permissions.github.manage: **Git Manager**: you also manage the Git sources (imports, sync, Rulesets mirror).
permissions.ai.manage: **AI manager**: you also configure the AI features and their models.
permissions.ai.use: **AI user**: you can use the AI assistant, rule analysis and generation.
permissions.rule.tag_any: **Tagger**: you can tag any rule, not only your own.
